content:
One of my favorite iPhone cases has returned with a fresh new look. I previously used earlier generations of BitmoLab's GAMEBABY case and fell in love at first sight. It feels like an accessory designed specifically to evoke my nostalgic feelings. The biggest selling point of this case is that it doesn't require additional accessories to carry and keep charged, but is a cleverly designed regular iPhone case that also doubles as a set of tactile physical buttons so you can play your beloved Game Boy ROMs (and other games). This is the perfect embodiment of "working smarter, not harder." It requires no battery or Bluetooth, and the setup process is extremely simple. If you're a fan of any form of retro game emulators, you must keep an eye on this product.

Check out our hands-on video to see how this case actually performs!

This case has a very simple yet ingenious design. It uses a two-piece design, with the lower half acting as a controller. During everyday non-gaming use, it feels just like a regular phone case. You get:

  • Tactile side buttons for the lock button, volume buttons, and action button
  • Cutouts for the USB-C port, speaker, buttons, and camera control
  • Protective bezels around the screen and camera module
  • Hard-shell plastic protection

But the magic is hidden in the lower half. That's where the game's control buttons are located, with excellent craftsmanship and a deeply satisfying tactile feel when pressed. But how exactly does it work?

How It Works

Again, the clever part is that it has no built-in electronic components whatsoever, so there's no pairing process required. How it works is that each physical game button features a small capacitive contact point that simulates the effect of your finger touching the screen. So the iPhone thinks you're tapping the on-screen control buttons, while it feels like you're pressing real buttons. This uses the same technology as the soft capacitive tips found on cheap stylus pens.

You'll need to perform a simple setup process to ensure the physical buttons align with the on-screen control positions. BitmoLabs provides all the necessary instructions via a QR code in the packaging. But it requires the Delta emulator app from the App Store to work. This app is completely free to use with zero in-app purchases. After downloading the app, GAMEBABY offers a downloadable custom interface skin that places the emulator's digital control buttons directly beneath the physical buttons. This skin is also free (you can download it even without the case).

Once the skin is installed in the Delta emulator app, you're ready to start gaming. You just detach the lower half of the case, flip it over, and reattach it to the iPhone. This way, the control buttons align with the screen, giving you the feel of real physical buttons when playing retro games. When you're done gaming, just slide out the controller portion, flip it back, and snap it back into place—and you have a regular phone case again.

My Experience Using It

As I mentioned in the introduction, I'm a slave to retro gaming—it triggers some deep-seated craving inside me that makes me want to replay the old Pokémon games from my younger days. This product not only makes gaming easier but delivers a nearly frictionless experience. I don't have to remember to bring any extra items, don't need to charge anything, and there's no pairing required. For me, remembering to bring one more accessory is often the biggest pain point with any tech accessory, and this case eliminates that hurdle.

You can also feel that BitmoLabs has significantly upgraded the build quality on this case. The buttons have excellent tactile feedback, snap back quickly when you release your fingers, and there's absolutely no key failure during gameplay. I mainly use it to revisit all the classic Pokémon titles, which are more casual-style games that don't require lightning-fast reflexes. Even for games requiring fast reactions, this case is more than capable.

There's one trade-off to note: no MagSafe support. Since the case uses a two-piece design with button components in the lower half, there's essentially no way to incorporate MagSafe functionality. So if you insist your phone case must have MagSafe, this product might not be for you. That said, if you have MagSafe accessories (I have quite a few myself), you just need to easily remove the case to use them. Additionally, there's no camera control button protective cover—it's not a big deal, but worth noting.

Pricing and Availability

GAMEBABY is now available on BitmoLab's official website and Amazon, starting at $24.99. Three versions are offered: GameBaby Color, GameBaby Retro, and the latest GameBaby Transparent (the version I'm showing here). GameBaby Transparent is only available for iPhone 17 Pro Max, with a limited production run of just 500 units, and can only be purchased from BitmoLab's official website. The remaining versions are compatible with iPhone 15 Pro and above, and can be bought from both Amazon and the official website. To reiterate, since there are no electronic components, batteries, or Bluetooth modules, they can keep the price down to $25, which is an absolute steal for a case like this!

Conclusion

If you're like me and enjoy revisiting retro games on your iPhone, this case is absolutely the perfect choice. It's affordable, lightweight and portable, easy to set up, and genuinely enhances the experience of playing retro emulator games on iPhone. Using the physical buttons together with iPhone's excellent haptic engine feels just like operating a real retro gaming console. With the recent wave of retro Pokémon game mod hype sweeping social media, now is the perfect time to relax and enjoy these games on your iPhone with physical buttons.

What do you think of this phone case? Would you consider getting one? Have you used one before? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments below!
